newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: U.S., two Koreas to discuss peace talks next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S., two Koreas to discuss peace talks next week.

text.p: Senior officials from the United States and North and South Korea will meet in New York on Monday to discuss steps to pave the way for four-nation peace talks, a South Korean foreign ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.
Spokesman Lee Kyu-hyung told reporters that officials at deputy minister-level would discuss concrete measures for a "preparatory meeting aimed at arranging four-way peace talks".

Seoul government sources said earlier on Wednesday the communist North had already agreed to hold the preparatory meeting in August. Those negotiations would involve senior officials from China as well as the three countries.

"An announcement is expected on the preparatory talks after the New York three-way meeting," Lee said. The four-way peace talks, proposed by U.S. President Bill Clinton and South Korean President Kim Young-sam last year, is designed to work out a peace settlement to replace the fraying ceasefire pact that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.

The New York contacts next week will be led by North Korean Vice Foreign Minister Kim Kye-gwan, South Korean Deputy Foreign Minister Song Young-shik and Chalres Kartman, acting assistant secretary at the U.S. State Department, Lee said.
